thread.title: Roadrunner: SumZero's Article Vs. My Take (50% Plus Upside) - Roadrunner Transportation Systems, Inc. (NYSE:RRTS)

author: Michael Wiggins De Oliveira
title: Roadrunner: SumZero's Article Vs. My Take (50% Plus Upside) - Roadrunner Transportation Systems, Inc. (NYSE:RRTS)
text:
Executive Summary I typically don't comment on research I see elsewhere, as I respect the point of view of others. However, given that SumZero's prestigious micro-cap award went to the LONG thesis for Roadrunner's ( RRTS ) I see no harm in highlighting where I agree and disagree with the analysis.
If you are reading this, I will assume that you are very familiar with Roadrunner's secondary offering already.
Where I Don't Agree With the Analysis I got this link on SA's free site, from one of the commentators . This article works best if you familiarize with the analyst's write-up on page 32 .
The analyst, which is clearly very talented, has a table on page 35. In this table, he calculates Elliott's implied EBITDA multiple on what he counts on the $45 million of cash injection (once the preferred $405 million is netted out). This is not fully accurate. Here is why.
Assume that, for the sake of discussion that many shareholders decide to buy to up the rights (which granted, is highly unlikely). Then, in this case, Elliott is only left with, say, 10% of the rights. Again, this is very much unlikely, but in this event, Elliott's implied equity value would reach $4.5 billion, which is nonsensical, I'm sure you'll agree?
Again, roughly the same can be said about the analyst's work on page 37, where those run-rate EBITDA's hit more than $299 million - seriously?
My expectation now is for the outcome to fall somewhere between Case 3 [EBITDA of $165m] and Case 4 [EBITDA should be around $470m]
- SumZero
Even if you don't follow anything else, you can objectively grasp that Roadrunner is not likely to, ever, have a run EBITDA of close to $300 million. Near-term, by FY 2020, management expects roughly $100 million of EBITDA, which appears reasonable by my own estimates.
Moving on, the analyst talks about Elliott ' break even on their $450m investment '. Again, this is incorrect. Elliott will have a made a huge sum of money through its make-even dividend of close to 17% on their preferred shares. That's exactly why Roadrunner is here in the first place! Elliott is not concerned about breaking even . Elliott is concerned about how much upside they can make.
What I Do Agree With Since I have been long Roadrunner, before reading the SumZero write up, one can easily expect me to have a strong behavioral bias towards the following two points. Sadly, there is little that can be done about this. Nevertheless, I think that once you see my two points, you too will largely fluctuate towards and agree with my highlights, even if you don't have a position in Roadrunner.
The most important outcome of the analysis is that the current stock price (with rights) has meaningful downside protection based on any combination of the outcome of the shareholding and Elliott’s intentions.
The above quote echoes my overall contention about Roadrunner: while the upside is indeed questionable, I fully believe that the downside is very much protected.
Finally, the analyst says:
Industry on a TTM basis trades in the range between 7x-10x and a de-levered, fundamentally improved RRTS should trade at least around the lower end of the multiple and slowly expand as management delivers results. This results in roughly a 76% upside.
This too, I have no real issue with.
The Main Risk To Roadrunner's Shareholders The analyst briefly touches on this. But in my words, my main worry is whether Elliott ends up holding up plus 90% of Roadrunner's common; and seeks to take Roadrunner private.
If that were to transpire, shareholders would be left with no upside what-so-ever. Having said that, in my opinion, Elliott would not want to take the company private as it would have to take it public again in order to realize any gain. Taking it private now, would only prolong Elliott's ability to realize their gain. But also, remember, Roadrunner is not the next Apple ( AAPL ) or Microsoft ( MSFT ).
Roadrunner is a very cyclical and somewhat capital intensive company. If I were Elliott, I would be looking to unwind Roadrunner's investment while times are good. A realistic scenario for Elliott
t will be out by mid-2020 (18 months). With more than 50% upside potential.
